summary: Taizan Maezumi was a Buddhist Studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, and SFSU, and trained under Hakujun Kuroda, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Koryu Osaka. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission and founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles.
Specializing in Sinology and religious studies, Tak Pui Sze completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

Taka Yanagisawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Japan Women's University (~1943–1948). She served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1982–1988).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Takahiko Kameyama has served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (both attested 2015).
Takahiko Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Takahiro Asano studied law at Chiba, social welfare at Doshisha and Washington University, and earned a PhD from York. Active in religious and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Japan Lutheran College (2021–2026) and Musashino University (2026).

Takahiro Kato is an Indology and philosophy scholar who holds a Dr.Phil from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg and serves as a professor at the University of Tokyo and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Takako Abe has served on the faculty at Taisho University, where she was a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Takamaro Shigaraki studied at Ryukoku University, UH Mānoa, and IBS. In Buddhist studies, he spent his career at Ryukoku University, becoming professor in 1970 and president (1989–1995), later serving as chairman of Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (1995–2008).

Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. He taught at Waseda Junior and Senior High School and later served as lecturer and Dean of the School of Letters at Waseda University.

Takami Inoue, a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology, was a doctoral candidate at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Takamichi Fukita studied at Taisho and Bukkyo universities under Zenno Ishigami, Shozen Kumoi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Heinz Bechert. He held a lectureship at Bukkyo University (attested 1999, 2013).

Takanobu Takahashi studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University. In Indology and linguistics, he held faculty posts at Shitennoji University and the University of Tokyo (1996; 1999–2016).
Takanori Fukita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University (attested 2017) and serves as a specially appointed lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

A scholar in religious studies and Japanology, Takanori Shintani studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977). He later held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1993–2009) and Kokugakuin University (~2009–2018).

Takanori Unno studied at Nagoya University under numerous mentors, including Hidenori Kitagawa and Yoshifumi Ueda. In Indology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Nagoya University (~1964–1973) and Meijo University (~1982–2007).

Takao Hayashi studied at Tohoku, Kyoto, and Brown universities, completing his PhD under David Pingree. A scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, he held appointments at Kyoto Women's University and served as professor at Doshisha University (1995–2015).
Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Takao Maruyama completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held professorships at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984; professor emeritus ~1995), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

Takao Moriyasu studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his doctorate from Osaka University. Focusing on Iranian/Central Asian studies and history, he served as professor at Osaka University (1994–2012) and later held posts at Kindai University and Toyo Bunko.
